subject: Next steps: data residency, logging, and model training exclusion
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Romero <lucia@medsyn.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up and confirmation items from today’s discovery

Hi Lucia —

Great to meet you and the MedSyn team earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) Training on customer data: you flagged that MedSyn requires that any customer data sent to Redwood for inference must not be used to improve models or for continued training. We can commit to a model-training opt-out for the duration of the contract and provide the contractual language for the DPA.

2) Data residency: you asked for EU data residency for logs and any persisted artifacts — we will surface options for regional routing and confirm the physical region for logs.

3) Logging & PII controls: you asked for minimized logging, PII redaction before storage, and a 30-day retention period for request logs. Marcus will share our redaction patterns and sample sanitized logs.

4) Evidence: I’m attaching the DPA draft and our most recent SOC2 report. Please review and flag needed edits.

Next steps: 
- Marcus: send sample redacted logs and implementation notes (ETA Fri 6/16).
- Neha: share initial commercial terms + DocuSign contract for legal review (ETA Mon 6/18).
- Lucia/Anita: confirm whether the 30-day retention and model-training opt-out are acceptable (reply to thread).

Thanks — I’ll keep this thread as the source of truth for privacy/contract items.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0179

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Medsyn_v1.2.pdf; SOC2-Type2-2028.pdf

From: Lucia Romero <lucia@medsyn.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Ghosh <anita.ghosh@medsyn.io>, Tom Baines <tom@medsyn.io>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up and confirmation items from today’s discovery

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the concise recap. Confirming MedSyn’s requirements: 

- Model training: MedSyn requires a strict opt-out: no customer data (structured or unstructured) will be used to train, fine-tune, or benchmark Redwood models. This must be explicit in the DPA and visible in the console for our admins.

- Retention: 30-day retention for request logs, then automatic purge. Short-term caches used for inference (KV cache) are allowed if they are ephemeral and never written to persistent storage.

- PII & redaction: Any logs retained must have PII redacted by Redwood prior to storage; we will provide a short list of sensitive fields (patient_id, national_id, full_ssn) for automatic masking.

- Residency: All persisted logs and admin audit records must be stored in an EU region (Ireland preferred).

We reviewed the SOC2 and DPA — overall fine, we’ll send redline requests if legal sees anything. Can you confirm: 1) a visible flag in the Redwood Console that indicates "Training Opt-Out Enabled" at the org level, and 2) a mechanism to receive an audit export showing retention/purge events?

Appreciate the quick turnaround. I’ve looped in Anita (legal) and Tom (platform) for their input.

— Lucia
Lucia Romero
Head of Product | MedSyn Health
lucia@medsyn.io

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Romero <lucia@medsyn.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:47:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up and confirmation items from today’s discovery

Hi Lucia —

Thanks — confirming technical answers below: 

- Training opt-out: We support an org-level opt-out which prevents ingestion of your requests into any model-improvement pipelines. That flag will be visible to admins in the Console and enforced in the control-plane.

- Audit exports: We can provide an audit export (CSV/JSON) listing retention/purge events and admin toggles. Exports can be scheduled or pulled on-demand; we’ll include an HMAC-signed manifest for verifiability.

- Data residency: We can pin storage to the eu-west-1 (Ireland) region for persisted logs and admin audit records. Ephemeral caches for inference will remain in the serving region but are not persisted.

- PII redaction: Attached is a small sample of the sanitized logs we plan to store (sample-redacted-logs.txt). Redaction is deterministic and configurable. If you provide the list of sensitive fields you mentioned, we’ll add them to the redaction ruleset.

I’ve attached the sample log and a short implementation note. Happy to run a quick tech sync next week if the team wants to validate the redaction behavior on a small test set.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Attachments: sample-redacted-logs.txt

From: Anita Ghosh <anita.ghosh@medsyn.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucia Romero <lucia@medsyn.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up and confirmation items from today’s discovery

Kimberly / Marcus —

Quick note from legal: the DPA clause language needs three small edits to explicitly state (1) no training for the duration of the agreement, (2) 30-day log retention with automated purge, and (3) EU-hosted storage for persisted logs. Please add a commitment to provide quarterly audit exports for the first year. If Redwood agrees to those edits, we can move DocuSign for the SOW + DPA.

Please send updated DPA with redlines and the Console screenshot for the training opt-out flag.

Regards,

Anita Ghosh
General Counsel | MedSyn Health
anita.ghosh@medsyn.io
